extracted.intended_audience: short story writers, anthology editors, and readers interested in contemporary American short fiction
extracted.subtask_description: Selecting and compiling the 'best' short stories published in American magazines during the previous year for inclusion in an annual anthology, with attention to literary quality, representativeness, and permissions. Includes producing paratextual Yearbook material (rolls of honor, distinctive lists, magazine addresses, biographical notes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — magazine publication in the previous year
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories eligible for inclusion are those "appearing in magazines during the previous year."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors selected these twenty stories from 118 American magazines — "from major national periodicals to the small literary quarterlies." Only pieces published in the eligible time window are considered; reprint permissions must be obtained from the original magazines/authors (see acknowledgments and copyright notices).

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic/national designation — 'American' authors and Canadians
rubrics_metrics.description: Anthology is titled 'American' but includes Canadian authors; foreword notes that Canadian authors "can be included" and references a court decision that Canadians are Americans for this purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While the focus is on stories that appeared in American magazines and that reflect American life, the editors explicitly allow inclusion of Canadian writers; by contrast many foreign authors appearing in American magazines could not be reprinted in a volume titled 'American.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Reflect specifically American experience
rubrics_metrics.description: Collection should "reflect[] our specifically American experience, our ways of life and consciousness."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection privileges stories that illuminate aspects of American society and consciousness — examples in the foreword include works probing black-white relationships, prison life, youth and coming-of-age crises, and regional life. The editors present examples of stories chosen for how they probe American social realities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Literary excellence — 'the best' and high standards
rubrics_metrics.description: The volume is described as a "distinguished annual collection of the best short stories," implying a quality-driven selection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors emphasize respect for the "highest standards in literature" (invoking journals like the Kenyon Review) and aim to "delight" readers and show "the latest developments in American short fiction." Selection is editorial and qualitative rather than formulaic; stories are chosen for their literary merit and impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and stylistic innovation as a positive criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: The foreword highlights recent developments and forms (vignettes, parodies, typographical experimentation, dream-centered stories) as notable trends worth attention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors note the "proliferation of the vignette," the popularity of parodies, prevalence of dream-centered narratives, and typographical experiments (e.g., Tillie Olsen). Such formal innovations are recognized as important features of contemporary short fiction and can factor into selection when they achieve artistic effect (e.g., a vignette having "the same emotional impact as the haiku").

rubrics_metrics.name: Universality of appeal over demographic pigeonholing
rubrics_metrics.description: "There is no such thing as a 'woman's story' or 'a man's story.' Or a 'child's story.' A good story can be enjoyed by any literate person. Thus there is no good 'black story.'"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors favor stories that transcend narrow demographic labels and have broad literary appeal; while they happily include works by writers of various identities (black authors, women, etc.), the primary evaluative lens is quality and universality rather than category-marked writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topical/social relevance and probing of difficult subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: Selected stories often confront social problems and intense topics — e.g., race relations, homosexuality in prison, psychotic depression, drug/violence encounters, political radicalization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Foreword examples show editors valuing stories that probe social relationships or illuminate harsh or complex scenes; topicality and the ability to "effectively illuminate a brutal scene" or present an "anguished search" are treated as merits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation of variety — authors' reputation and newcomer balance
rubrics_metrics.description: The anthology includes both well-known writers and newcomers; selections are made from a wide range of periodicals and aim to show the breadth of current short fiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors deliberately select from both major national magazines and small quarterlies and include a mixture of established award-winning authors and original new voices (the contents list includes National Book Award winners and first-time appearances in certain magazines).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rights and permissions requirement for reprinting
rubrics_metrics.description: Reprinting requires permission; the volume contains acknowledgments granting reprint rights from magazines and authors and lists copyright notices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each story's reprint is accompanied by a credit line naming the original publication and copyright holder; editors only reprint upon receiving permission and give explicit acknowledgments in a dedicated section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paratextual Yearbook features as editorial apparatus
rubrics_metrics.description: The book includes a Yearbook section (Roll of Honor, Distinctive Short Stories, Addresses of American and Canadian Magazines, Biographical Notes) that functions as part of the editors' curatorial standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These supplementary lists and notes serve to document the year's notable stories and sources, provide further reading and contact information, and signal additional selection judgments (e.g., 'Distinctive Short Stories' and 'Roll of Honor' identify works and outlets the editors regard as meritorious beyond the twenty reprinted pieces).

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial outreach and curation process
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors solicit copies from magazine editors and encourage new magazines to send their issues to be considered for future volumes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The foreword explicitly urges new magazine editors to send copies to the anthology editors — indicating a proactive curation and scouting process across the magazine ecosystem as part of selection practice.
